question.problem:
The population $P(t)$ of elk in a protected national park follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=5P-0.001{P}^{2},\,P(0)=200,
$$

where $t$ is the time, measured in years. For which value of $P$ is the elk population growing at the fastest possible rate?

$P=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{P}^{′}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

For a logistic growth model, the fastest rate of growth occurs when $P=\frac{1}{2}a.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14200098/assets/9019b26b417c757bbfab79afb39379c1fc7a892bc44e934c6f23c339deacfd68.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{dt} & =5P-0.001{P}^{2} \\  & =0.001P(5000-P)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=5000.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $5000,$ and $P$ grows at its fastest possible rate when 

$$
P=\frac{1}{2}a=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5000=2500.
$$
